meaning:
τελευτάω, -ῶ
(τελευτή), [in LXX chiefly for מוּת ;]
1. trans., to complete, finish; esp. τ. τ. αἰῶνα, τ. βίον, to complete life, to die (Æsch., Hdt., al.).
2. Intrans., to come to an end, hence, to die (Hdt., al.): Mat.2:19 9:18 22:25, Mrk.9:48, Luk.7:2, Jhn.11:39, Act.2:29 7:15, Heb.11:22; Hebraistically, θανάτῳ τελευτάτω (מוּת, Exo.21:17), Mat.15:4, Mrk.7:10" (LXX) .†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”
“Brothers, I may tell you freely of the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
By faith, Joseph, when his end was near, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel, and gave instructions concerning his bones.
